newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up 8.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up 8.25 percent.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index soared 8.25 percent in heavy trading on Wednesday, with more and more institutions scrambling to build positions on expectations Beijing will announce market-boosting policies, brokers said.
The B index surged 8.48 points to close at its intraday high of 111.35, with turnover swelling to HK$119.95 million from HK$81.40 million on Tuesday.
Brokers said the rise was due to rumours that securities regulators are considering market-boosting measures.
"Institutions are increasing their positions, expecting regulators to implement policies in the near future to boost the market," a local analyst said.
"B shares appear very undervalued, following a long slump and a bull run in the A share market since April," said a broker at Shenzhen J&A Securities.
Because the B index has gained about 25 percent over the past few sessions, profit-taking is likely to set in later this week, one analyst cautioned.
More overseas investors are being attracted to the market, the analyst said.
The market's medium-term trend should be decided by whether regulators announce stimulative policies by the end of this year and the 1996 results of B share listed firms, analysts said.
Large-cap issues remained the focus of trading, they said.
China Bicycle, the day's star, surged HK$0.71, or 35.68 percent, to HK$2.70 on trade of 1.11 million shares due to speculative demand by institutions, brokers said.
Dadonghai followed suit, rising HK$0.55, or 30.56 percent, to HK$2.35 after 6.36 million shares changed hands.
Jiangling Motors was the third largest gainer, up HK$0.51, or 22.27 percent, to HK$2.80 on volume of 519,000 shares.

Changan Automobile, the most active counter, put on HK$0.22 to HK$2.28, with 9.65 million shares traded. Profit-taking sent Vanke down HK$0.15 to HK$5.55 and Guangdong Power HK$0.05 down to HK$5.40, brokers said.
The A share index maintained its bull run, rising 13.84 points, or 3.10 percent, to end at a record high of 460.83.
Turnover rose to a record 18.82 billion yuan from the previous session's 16.62 billion yuan.
The composite index added 13.58 points, or 3.27 percent, to finish at 429.37.
